title: Market Crash Deep Dive Analysis
summary: Shutdown stress, liquidity failures and selective buying.
coverage_note: All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

claims.reason: Darden and Carnival show the concrete channel: fixed cash obligations persisted while revenue collapsed, forcing financing and payout cuts. This supports amplification, not the claim debt alone caused the pandemic recession.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: 2020 annual report
evidence.finding: Pandemic response included full revolver draw, $270 million term loan, equity offering and dividend suspension. Q4 sales declined 43%; company survived but changed its financing structure.

evidence.title: Fiscal 2020 Form 10-K
evidence.finding: FY 2020 net loss was $10.236 billion, versus $2.990 billion profit in 2019. Weighted average shares rose from 690 million to 775 million. Dividend stopped after first quarter; financing restricted future payments.

claims.reason: The Fed expanded dramatically in 2020, supporting the near-term policy direction. A decade-wide historical analogy includes fiscal, exchange-rate and institutional differences and remains incomplete; it is not a precise repeated-cycle model.

evidence.finding: Weekly total assets rose from $4.183 trillion on February 12, 2020 to $4.242 trillion March 4 and $6.368 trillion April 15. A brief late-February decline preceded the surge.

claims.claim: Oil faces demand and supply shocks
claims.reason: EIA verifies the demand/storage shock and severe futures dislocation. The relative contribution of announced Saudi/Russian supply increases requires production data; this article describes rivalry more accurately than the earlier coordination claim.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

evidence.title: Low liquidity and limited storage pushed WTI futures below zero
evidence.finding: May WTI futures traded below zero on April 20 amid the demand collapse, expiring contract and limited storage. Positive deferred and other benchmark prices mean this was not all oil trading below zero.

evidence.title: Brent spot crude price
evidence.finding: Daily USD/barrel observations: 69.08 on January 3, 2020; 9.12 on April 21, 2020; 78.61 on December 30, 2021; 82.82 on December 30, 2022. These are spot prices, not futures-investment returns.

framework_lessons: Stress revenue interruption and financing access together.
assessment: Useful anticipation of further equity losses and dividend cuts coexists with a wrong next-week dollar call and a wrong Tractor Supply demand expectation. The distinction between a liquid business and a surviving shareholder remains central. Speculative explanations of specific market flows stay unverified.
